aspects.says: Security tokens are compared in constant time, never returning at the first differing character; an early return on length leaks only the public length.
ObjectInputStream runs class code while it rebuilds untrusted bytes; avoid it, or set a JEP 290 filter that allow-lists every class in the graph.
basis: section:5. Using Java serialization for untrusted data
section:Software and Data Integrity Failures (OWASP 2021 A08)

aspects.says: A failed login gets one generic message, so it never reveals whether the username or the password was wrong.
basis: section:3. Revealing authentication details in error messages

aspects.says: Very long inputs are capped to prevent ReDoS, and null bytes are stripped.
aspects.reason: bounded input is practised on 10.6.1 (bounded-read, signup-validation); the page gives no rule precise enough to grade here

aspects.says: Account lockout stops brute force: after N failures the account is locked for a period, and a success resets the count.
Usernames are normalized, for example to lower case, before comparison so capitalisation cannot bypass a check.
XSS is prevented by encoding output for the context it is rendered in: &, <, >, " and ' become HTML entities at the point of rendering.
basis: section:2. Rendering user input directly in HTML

aspects.says: Encoding belongs to output, for the context the data is rendered in, not to input on its way into storage.
The OWASP Top 10 groups the risks: injection, broken authentication and access control, sensitive data exposure, and integrity failures such as insecure deserialization.
aspects.reason: an overview; each category's Java defence is practised in its own practice on this page

aspects.says: Parameterized queries carry values only; identifiers and keywords such as an ORDER BY column or direction are chosen from an allow-list.
Passwords are stored as salted slow hashes (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2), never in plain text.
aspects.reason: 10.6.3 teaches why a fast hash is wrong for passwords (its quiz asks what SHA-256 alone suits); bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2 need libraries the practice build does not carry

aspects.says: Role-based access control maps roles to permissions, is enforced at the service layer and denies by default.
aspects.reason: permission checks before a call are practised in 42-annotations 10.4.2 (role-access) and 10.4.4 (secured-proxy)

aspects.says: SQL injection is a query construction problem: PreparedStatement sends parameters separately from the SQL, so they are never read as code.
basis: section:1. Using string concatenation for SQL queries

aspects.says: Writing SQL as a text block avoids escape bugs but values must still be bound as PreparedStatement parameters.
CSP headers, HttpOnly and Secure cookies, CSRF tokens, a WAF and updated dependencies add layers of defence.
